content:
maria: Quick heads-up — we're proposing to prune the freeform `event.attrs` blob and extract a compacted attrs table `route_metrics_attrs_v2` for console/analytics. Primary goals: reduce storage, make per-route metric queries faster, and un-block per-tenant quota rollups.

sam: +1 on the intent. main worry is dashboard queries that still reference attrs via JSON path. how do we keep those queries working during rollout?

lee: We can add a read-adapter that checks v2 first then falls back to v1. cheap to add at API layer. will add slight latency but avoids big backfills.

maria: Exactly. Plan sketch: 1) dual-write into attrs_v2 for new events, 2) add read-adapter in console query layer, 3) backfill historical data gradually with a priority window for top customers, 4) GC old blob after rollouts.

ana: typo — you mean @ana? :slightly_smiling_face:

ana: oops — meant ana.

ana (ana): For backfill we should compute compact attributes for routes with > 1k p50 traffic first. Others can be lazy. Also need to version the attribute schema (v2) so downstream dashboards know how to map fields.

maria: Good call on versioning. Also considering adding a `route_attr_version` field on route_metrics so console can short-circuit mapping.

sam: Performance notes: the new attrs table will be hot for route_id lookups. Need an index on (route_id, attr_key) and maybe a composite for time-window queries. We should model access patterns before choosing pk.

lee: Agreed. Query patterns: dashboard widgets do route_id + last_7d aggregation, quota engine does route_id + quota_window. Proposed DDL snippet:

sam: ```sql
CREATE TABLE route_metrics_attrs_v2 (
  route_id UUID,
  attr_key TEXT,
  attr_value TEXT,
  bucket_ts TIMESTAMP,
  created_at TIMESTAMP,
  route_attr_version INT,
  PRIMARY KEY ((route_id), attr_key, bucket_ts)
);
CREATE INDEX ON route_metrics_attrs_v2 (route_id, bucket_ts);
```

maria: That looks reasonable. Also need TTL for attrs — many are ephemeral. we'll tie GC to tenant retention policy.

tarek: Ops concern: dual-write increases write QPS & doubles storage temporarily. We should gate dual-write with a feature flag per-host so Dedicated customers can opt-in slower. Also track write failures and circuit-break to avoid blocking ingestion.

maria: We'll implement dual-write with non-blocking fallback: if v2 write fails, log metric and continue. No blocking. We'll also have a canary where dual-write is enabled for 5% of traffic to validate indexes/latency.

ana (ana): For dashboards we need to provide a mapping layer -> a simple transform spec file: key mapping and type coercions. product can add UI toggle to switch to v2 mapping for preview.

sam: Backfill strategy: parallel workers that read v1 blobs, emit rows into v2. Backfill window prioritized by tenant usage. We'll publish a progress table for rollout visibility.

migrate-bot: migration-job-1782345690 started: scanning 0/5000 routes (canary set). ETA ~2h.

lee: We should add a query-time fallback that emits a telemetry metric when fallback occurs so we can find remaining consumers of v1.

maria: Agreed. Also add regression alerts: any dashboard query p95 increase > 20% flagged.

tarek: One more ops note: ensure compaction and GC jobs have rate limits; otherwise we risk throttling analytics store during heavy backfills.

ana (ana): I'm going to draft the mapping spec and a small migration README. will ping product for UI toggle mock.

maria: Thanks — next steps: ana draft spec, sam/lee finalize index design, tarek build canary gate + ops runbook, I'll schedule a 30m sync tomorrow.

sam: ack.

lee: ack, will mock query adapter PR.

maria: Closing loop: keep thread updated with any perf numbers from the canary. :thumbsup:
